speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis of the hip presenting as knee pain/swelling).

The patient is an 18-month-old male with unilateral knee swelling, no trauma, and a family history suggestive of a genetic predisposition; this presentation is classic for Perthes disease, where hip pathology often refers pain to the knee. I will confirm this by examining the hip range of motion and ordering imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Xray_and_Hip_Ultrasound.
